This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **2** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4a5396b81e0666dc4c71d13394a32e59ed411a48` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `055c30915d41654851883507bb1528287e23cb84` — the merge of head `6840f48cab7173ab94431a1a8c3b9b5af8bcc201` into base `4a5396b81e0666dc4c71d13394a32e59ed411a48`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 055c30915d41654851883507bb1528287e23cb84 && git checkout 055c30915d41654851883507bb1528287e23cb84
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4a5396b81e0666dc4c71d13394a32e59ed411a48 6840f48cab7173ab94431a1a8c3b9b5af8bcc201 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4a5396b81e0666dc4c71d13394a32e59ed411a48 && git merge --no-ff 6840f48cab7173ab94431a1a8c3b9b5af8bcc201

```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6840f48cab7173ab94431a1a8c3b9b5af8bcc201`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.test.ts, .changeset/27402-mcp-include-refuses.md, content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx + packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-connector.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/connector-mcp-plugin.ts, packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-provider.ts, packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-provider.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/spec/src/integration/connector.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider.ts, docs/adr/0097-declarative-connector-instances.md

Read at 2026-10-30T06:37Z: card #27402 (body and all 7 comments, above all triage 6489254710, claim 6515507103 with amendments 6515533290 and 6515646431, os-dev-report 6516451168), PR #27985 (body, 4-file list, both comments, Contract-review-claim 6516467804), the net diff of the head against main (4 files, +230/−3), the head's check-runs, and the cited code at the head. Adversarial read; the seat's conclusions were not taken as inputs.

### ① Derived judgments

**Fail-closed, every shape traced through the factory at the head.** The predicate is: refuse when `include` is not `undefined` and is either not an array or has an entry that is not a non-empty string. So `include: 'web_search'` (string), an object, `null`, a `Set`, a boxed string, `['web_search', 7]`, `['web_search', '']` are all refused before any client is created (the client factory is never called; the test pins `connected === false`). Explicit `include: undefined` reads as absent, which is the openapi provider's reading too and the only reading JSON metadata can carry. `include: []` passes the shape check, the predicate denies every tool, the unknown set is empty, and the instance materializes with zero actions: the closed direction, as openapi. Whitespace variants, case variants and typos pass the shape check and are then refused after `tools/list` as unknown entries (exact-match against the names the server listed); duplicates are collapsed through a `Set` before the unknown check, so `['web_search', 'nope', 'nope']` names `'nope'` once. A paginating server is not a hole: `McpClientLike.listTools()` is contracted to return every page, and the default client follows `nextCursor` up to the 100-page bound and otherwise throws, which `createMcpConnector` closes the client on and the factory classifies upstream-unavailable, so the predicate always sees the whole list or no instance exists. A `tools/list` that throws is unchanged (closed by `createMcpConnector`, rethrown as upstream-unavailable or credential-rejected); one that returns nothing with a non-empty `include` is refused with every entry named. No path yields every tool once `include` is present.

**No leaked client on the refusal path.** Shape refusal: no client. Unknown-entry refusal: `bundle.close()` is awaited, its own rejection swallowed, before the throw; the unknown-entry test pins `closed === true`, the listed-tools test pins `closed === false`; the dev's third ablation leg (close deleted, 1 failure) proves the pin is live.

**Fidelity to openapi, read side by side.** Shape predicate: identical (`raw === undefined` passes; `!Array.isArray(raw) || raw.some(not a non-empty string)` refuses). Fault class: both a plain `Error`, so neither `isConnectorUpstreamUnavailable` nor `isConnectorCredentialRejected` matches, and the materializer's `fail()` branch takes it. Message skeleton: `connector-NAME provider: connector 'X' providerConfig.include must be an array of … (strings): each …` and `… providerConfig.include names 'a', 'b', which the … does not …. Each entry must be …; the … N …: 'k1', 'k2'…, … M more.` with the same sample of 20 and the same `… N more` tail. Timing: openapi validates shape after its `baseUrl` check and before the document fetch; mcp validates after transport normalization and the stdio policy and before connecting. Both check unknown entries after the upstream list is in hand, through the same device (the generator's own `include` predicate records every offered key as it filters). The one asymmetry is necessary: mcp holds a live connection at that point and closes it; openapi holds none.

**Materializer and the "rejected with the reason" clause.** `reconcileDeclaredConnectors` (service-automation `plugin.ts`) catches the factory's throw, strips credential forms, and routes: credential-rejected → hold; upstream-unavailable → degrade; anything else → `fail('[Automation] failed to materialize connector instance NAME via provider mcp (ADR-0097).', thrown)`, which at boot throws with the cause appended (the kernel boot test pins both halves of that message) and on reload logs at `error` and skips the entry. The teardown of a previous bundle happens only after a successful re-materialization, so on reload the prior valid connector keeps serving. That is the openapi provider's exact path and ADR-0097's recorded reconcile rule, and the docs page's reload table row says the same. There is no `rejected` instance state anywhere in the materializer; the word names a credential-row status. See ③ for what that leaves open.

**Spec.** `providerConfig` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` with the describe text "validated by the provider factory at boot"; ADR-0097 §2 places validation in the factory. No schema moves; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is the right kind because an authorable value an author could write is now refused where that value is judged.

**Tests.** Every refusal is pinned through the real `createMcpProviderFactory` with an injected client that lists `web_search` + `delete_everything`, each asserting a plain fault (not upstream, not credential), the first sentence of the message, and the connection fact. The control (no `include` → both tools) and the positive case (`['web_search']` → exactly that tool, not closed) are present. One pin runs through the real door: LiteKernel + AutomationServicePlugin + ConnectorMcpPlugin with a declared instance carrying a string `include` fails `bootstrap()` with the materializer's message plus the include message and never connects. Red-first 8 failed / 26 passed on base with the fix stashed; green 34/34; the 3-leg ablation isolates distinct assertion sets (shape off → 6, unknown off → 2, close off → 1), so each leg is meaningful.

**Gates and dogfood.** Check-runs on the head at this read: 33 success, 14 skipped, 6 in progress (Test Core shards 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8). Green: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate, PR-body guards. The dogfood battery is on record at this head: os-dev-report 6516451168 names the head's short id with command-exit 0, 357 files passed / 3 skipped, 2875 tests passed / 20 skipped; the head's merge commit was made at 2026-10-30T05:57Z and the report posted at 2026-10-30T06:24Z, which fits the 1435 s hold it reports. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing was re-run here.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/connector-mcp: minor` is right. The kind is `narrowed` (a value an author can write is now refused), and a protocol kind takes at least minor on the package the diff moves; no major (the dev's `check-changeset-no-major` reading, and the Check Changeset run is green). The changeset carries the `!` title, the BREAKING banner, Before / Now / Who sees it / The remedy, both line-initial declarations (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`), and one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, which is the honest disposition: a conversion rewriting a string into a one-element array would be the lenient alias the #26709 ruling refuses ("one meaning for `include`"), and an unknown tool name has no mechanical TO. The category is in the gate's `CATEGORIES` and ADR-0087's examples; the identical form with a "The remedy" paragraph landed on #27541. Precedent for the level: the openapi `include` changeset on #27387 was minor as `added`. PR body and changeset declarations agree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation from the triage wording, accepted.** Triage 6489254710 (2026-10-29T06:00Z) says "leave the instance `rejected` with the reason". No such instance state exists; the PR lands the clause as the configuration-fault path, exactly as openapi: boot fails naming the instance and the reason; a reload logs the reason at `error` and skips the entry. The dispatch's file surface excluded the materializer, and "exactly as `openapi` does" governs. The dev disclosed it in the acceptance notes.
- **Finding for the seat to file (outside the surface; both providers).** A configuration fault that first surfaces during a degraded-instance backoff retry (server down at boot → husk; server up later → an `include` entry it does not list) reaches the soft `fail()` branch, which logs and continues but leaves `degradedInstances` and the registered husk untouched: `GET /connectors` keeps the stale "could not reach its MCP server" reason, the dispatch refusal keeps promising an automatic retry, and the timer reconnects every 5 minutes against a fault no retry can clear. Location: `reconcileDeclaredConnectors`, the catch's plain-error branch. Class: ADR-0097 contract (configuration faults are not retried). Fail-closed holds throughout; nothing is exposed. The openapi provider has the same gap (a spec URL transiently down at boot).
- **Open policy question (ruling, not this PR).** On a reload, an edit that *adds* `include` to remove a destructive tool but mis-spells it fails to re-materialize, and ADR-0097's reconcile rule keeps the previous, wider connector serving, with the error logged. That is the rule as written and openapi behaves the same; whether a failed narrowing should degrade instead is for the ADR.
- **Spec stays open by design.** `providerConfig` is an open record and no publish-time lint reads `include`'s shape, so the first signal for a string `include` is boot or reload. ADR-0097 §2 puts the validation in the factory; noted, not a defect of this PR.
- **Out of scope, confirmed stale at the head (skills lane; the seat files it).** `skills/objectstack-automation/references/integration-recipes.md:63` and `skills/objectstack-automation/evals/integrations-declared.json:7` still say the openapi provider has no `include` key. The MCP recipe in the same file writes `include: ['search_issues']` and stays valid.
- **Declared deviation, cosmetic.** The PR-body footer carries the card-thread session link plus the harness block, with the `Fixes #27402` line under the attribution block; the recognisers read the line-initial declarations and the PR-body guards are green.
- **Docs drift check** listed no page ("not a clean bill of health"); the hand re-read here covers the `provider: 'mcp'` section and the reload table row of the same page, both consistent with the code.
- Six Test Core shards were still running at the read; the Tier S landing waits on every check being green regardless of this record.

### ④ Design judgment

- **packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts** — holds against `createMcpConnector` (one `include` call per listed tool, so the recorded list is the whole list), against the openapi provider it mirrors, and against the materializer's `fail()` branch. No must-fix. Should-fix (low, parity nits): name the sample size as a constant as openapi's `INCLUDE_REFUSAL_KEY_SAMPLE` does instead of a bare literal with a comment; and let the `McpProviderConfig.include` member doc say what the factory doc now says, as openapi's interface doc does.
- **packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.test.ts** — the refusals are pinned at the factory with the connection facts, the control is present, the ablation is meaningful. No must-fix. Should-fix: (a) pin `include: []` → zero actions and a materialized instance, the claim the PR body makes and the openapi test names mcp for, with no mcp pin on the head; (b) pin the unknown-entry refusal through the real boot as openapi does (`bootstrap()` rejects with the names-entry message and `getConnectorDegradedReason('vendor_mcp')` is undefined, so the fault fails rather than degrades), and tighten the string-shape boot test's tail, whose `descriptor?.actions ?? []` would pass vacuously if the engine were absent.
- **.changeset/27402-mcp-include-refuses.md** — level, banner, declarations, disposition and remedy hold against the rule and the two precedents. No must-fix, no should-fix.
- **content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx** — the new paragraph states the shape refusal before connecting, the unknown-entry refusal after listing, the never-every-tool guarantee and the absent-means-every-tool default, matching the code and the openapi paragraph above it; the page's existing reload row carries the reload semantics. No must-fix, no should-fix.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 维护者速读(席位终稿)

- **改了什么**：声明式 `provider: 'mcp'` 连接器的 `providerConfig.include` 写错时，实例不再静默暴露服务端的全部工具。有两种拒收：`include` 不是非空字符串数组时，连接前就拒收；条目点名了服务端 `tools/list` 里没有的工具时，列出后拒收（先关连接）。两种都按普通配置错误处理，消息形状与 `openapi` provider（#27387）一致。
- **为什么改**：`include` 是作者用来把危险工具挡在 flow 和 agent 之外的白名单。以前少打一对方括号（写成字符串），就会暴露全部工具，任何地方都不报错。
- **风险与回滚**：受影响的只有 `include` 写错的实例：启动时会失败，热重载时会记错误日志并跳过该条，旧实例照旧服务（ADR-0097 的 reconcile 规则，与 openapi 相同）。回滚 = revert 本 PR。
- **先看**：`packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts` 的 `createMcpProviderFactory`。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/connector-mcp exec vitest run src/mcp-provider.test.ts`。
- **需要你做的**：无，由席位落地。

**席位意见:** ACCEPT。收窄与 openapi 逐项对齐，所有探过的形状都失败即关闭，契约复核 PASS。

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · head `6840f48cab7173ab94431a1a8c3b9b5af8bcc201` · 2026-10-30T06:40Z

- **形态:** 4 files (+230/−3): `createMcpProviderFactory`, its tests, the changeset, and the mcp section of `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` (claim amendment 6515646431). Tier S. No `packages/spec`.
- **Clause-②:** `no (narrowing)`. The title has `!`, the changeset has a BREAKING banner, `minor` on `@objectstack/connector-mcp`, and ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`.
- **前提实测:** the card's three shapes reproduced red before the fix (8 red), per the os-dev-report 6516451168.
- **抽查读数:** contract review 6516635534 PASS on this head. Fail-closed holds for every probed shape (string, object, null, empty or non-string entries, case/whitespace typos, duplicates, paginated or throwing `tools/list`). `include: []` gives zero tools. No client is leaked on either refusal. Parity with openapi: the same predicate, fault class, message skeleton and timing. Narrowing dogfood battery at this head: 357 files passed, 2875 tests passed.
- **门禁 check-runs:** 54 on this head: 40 success, 14 skipped, 0 other (read 2026-10-30T06:40Z). Derived gates 87/87 exit 0, 0 NOT-MEASURED.
- **接受的偏差:** the review's three non-blocking should-fixes: no unit pin for `include: []`; the unknown-entry refusal is pinned at the factory, not through a LiteKernel boot, and the string-shape boot test's tail can pass vacuously; parity nits (sample-size constant, `include` member JSDoc). Triage's "`rejected` with the reason" maps to the configuration-fault path, because no `rejected` instance state exists outside credential rows. The dev disclosed this, and openapi does the same. The PR body's attribution footer names the card thread's session.
- **范围外去向:** #27992 (a configuration fault first seen on a degraded instance's backoff retry leaves a stale degraded state, on both providers; it also carries the reload policy question). #27987 (skills text and its eval say openapi has no `include`).
- **散文面:** the changeset, the connectors.mdx section and the refusal messages, read by the seat and the review.
- **落地条款:** relay `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the merge queue.
